learning_objective: 🎯 Analyze the heartbreaking contrast between wealthy city dwellers and impoverished rural folk, and the false promises made by politicians to the poor.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: लौकी या कद्दू की तरह की सब्जी
होश खो बैठना / सोचने की क्षमता खोना

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A poor farmer has set up a small roadside stand on a highway, hoping that rich city people driving by will stop and buy some wild berries or squash, giving them a little money to improve their lives.

The polished city traffic speeds by without stopping. If they ever stop, it is only to complain about the badly painted 'N' and 'S' signs ruining the landscape, or to ask for gas (which the stand doesn't sell).
The rural people don't just want a few coins; they want a share of the city's wealth and prosperity that the movies promise them but the political party in power denies them.

The poet criticizes politicians and businessmen ('greedy good-doers', 'beasts of prey') who pretend to help rural people by moving them into villages near theaters and stores, only to exploit them and make them lazy.

The poet can't bear the 'childish longing in vain'—the sight of the farmer waiting all day at the window for a car to stop. He fantazises about putting these poor people out of their misery in one stroke, but realizes it's an irrational thought.

fun_activity.title: 🛑 Stop and Empathize
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you are driving a fancy car past this roadside stand. Instead of speeding past, you stop. Write a 2-line dialogue of what you would kindly say to the farmer selling wild berries.

exam_tips: 📌 Focus on the oxymorons: 'Greedy good-doers' and 'beneficent beasts of prey'. These highlight the hypocrisy of politicians who pretend to help but actually exploit the poor.
📌 The 'childish longing' refers to the innocent but hopeless wait of the farmers for city cars to stop and buy their goods.
📌 Understand the tone: The poet feels immense empathy for the villagers and deep anger towards the insensitive city dwellers.
quick_recap: ⭐ The rural folk are begging for 'city money' so they can experience the lifestyle shown in motion pictures.
⭐ The city people complain that the clumsy paint of the stand 'marred' (ruined) the beauty of the mountain landscape.
⭐ 'Teaching them how to sleep' means the exploiters drug the poor into a false sense of security while robbing them of their self-reliance.
